o: The wickedness of the land. The fearful vengeance to be executed.
These judgments to be inflicted by a nation more wicked than themselves.
bg: Embrace, the eighth of the twelve minor prophets. Of his personal history we have no reliable information.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The wickedness of the land. The fearful vengeance to be executed (vv. 1–11); These judgments to be inflicted by a nation more wicked than themselves (vv. 12–17). People named: Habakkuk.
ch.mh: The servants of the Lord are deeply afflicted by seeing ungodliness and violence prevail; especially among those who profess the truth.
q: Read verses 1–11 (The wickedness of the land. The fearful vengeance to be executed). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 12–17 (These judgments to be inflicted by a nation more wicked than themselves), what do you learn about judgment?
Verse 12 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Deuteronomy 32:4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Habakkuk’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of sin and repentance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Habakkuk?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us remember, whatever advantages we possess, we must give all the glory to God.
ch.a: Let the seriousness of God's judgment move you to examine your ways and to pray for others.

bg: Embrace, the eighth of the twelve minor prophets. Of his personal history we have no reliable information.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Habakkuk must wait in faith (vv. 1–4); Judgments upon the Chaldeans (vv. 5–14); Also upon drunkenness and idolatry (vv. 15–20). Places: Lebanon.
ch.mh: When tossed and perplexed with doubts about the methods of Providence, we must watch against temptations to be impatient.
q: Read verses 1–4 (Habakkuk must wait in faith). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–14 (Judgments upon the Chaldeans), what do you learn about sin and repentance?
Verse 3 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Psalms 27:14. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
Where do you see the theme of worship and praise in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Habakkuk?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: When we have poured out complaints and requests before God, we must observe the answers God gives by his word, his Spirit, and providences; what the Lord will say to our case.
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.

o: The prophet beseeches God for his people.
He calls to mind former deliverances.
His firm trust in the Divine mercy.
bg: Embrace, the eighth of the twelve minor prophets. Of his personal history we have no reliable information.

Abounding in foliage, or abounding in caverns, (Gen. 21:21), a desert tract forming the north-eastern division of the peninsula of Sinai, lying between the Arabah on the east and the wilderness of Shur on the west. It is intersected in a north-western direction by the Wady el-Arish.

Probably a poetic or prolonged name of the land of Cush, the Arabian Cush (Hab. 3:7). Some have, however, supposed this to be the same as Chushan-rishathaim (Judg. 3:8, 10), i.e., taking the latter part of the name as a title or local appellation, Chushan "of the two iniquities" (= oppressing Israel, and provoking them to idolatry), a Mesopotamian king, identified by Rawlinson with Asshur-ris-ilim (the father of Tigl

A place in Southern Idumea, the land of "the sons of the east," frequently mentioned in the Old Testament. It was noted for the wisdom of its inhabitants (Amos 1:12; Obad. 1:8; Jer. 49:7; Ezek. 25:13).
ch.s: This chapter covers: The prophet beseeches God for his people (vv. 1,2); He calls to mind former deliverances (vv. 3–15); His firm trust in the Divine mercy (vv. 16–19). People named: Habakkuk, Teman, Midian. Places: Paran, Cushan.
ch.mh: The word prayer seems used here for an act of devotion.
q: Read verses 1,2 (The prophet beseeches God for his people). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 3–15 (He calls to mind former deliverances), what do you learn about salvation and redemption?
Verse 18 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Job 13:15. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Habakkuk’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of worship and praise in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Habakkuk?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: In the hope of a heavenly crown, let us sit loose to earthly possessions and comforts, and cheerfully bear up under crosses.
ch.a: Thank God for His deliverance, and share what He has done for you with one person.
